paper_title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
core_problem: Language models suffer from inherent limitations such as an inability to access up-to-date information, execute precise calculations, or interact with external tools.
methodology_summary: A self-supervised approach where the language model samples candidate API calls, executes them to get results, filters calls based on whether their output reduces perplexity on subsequent tokens, and fine-tunes itself on the resulting augmented dataset.
empirical_results: Demonstrates strong zero-shot and few-shot performance across various natural language tasks, outperforming larger baseline models by effectively integrating API call outputs into token predictions.
explicit_limitations: Toolformer still lags behind state-of-the-art models on certain benchmarks, fails to trigger tool usage in a significant portion of relevant cases, and may suffer from noise introduced during training on synthetic API-augmented datasets.
